meeting_flow.opening_phrase: I thought I'd start just by understanding a bit on your current situation with the property, then we can go through some figures in our service, see if it runs on what you're looking for.
meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: So I can go through some figures, then I can go through how the service works and sort of what is left for us to deal with, what we need from you.
meeting_flow.income_intro: So we're looking at gross revenue, so this is what a guest pays in total. About 65,000 a year. It's about 5,400 a month.
meeting_flow.how_it_works_transition: So I'll go through a bit about how the management works. So the first part is what we cover and then what we need from your end.
meeting_flow.meeting_2_ask: I'll send everything to you in the next half hour... and then we'll touch base in a couple of months if you've got any questions.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: So that's fine. That's why I'm finding really confusing. So if the guest is paying the cleaning, why are we paying the cleaning as well?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Because this figure is what a guest pays in total for a booking... this is what a guest is paying, and then this is what the owner sort of gets in terms of net revenue.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: In total, okay. Fine. Fine... so it's basically a pass through.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: I'm very surprised because it really needs to because I think the July potential is massive because of Silverstone.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: I think that's the place it's got picked up... it's showing a peak, but I might have expected it to be a bit more.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Accepted that pricing already reflects a July peak, moved on

lead_responses.what_lead_said: You know, how likely are we to get potential corporate lets or people who are using it for a longer period because we're right by all the Formula One teams... then you've got less people to leave reviews. It's the counter argument, I guess.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Direct booking potential is about 80 out of 100... you save on commissions by quite a lot, so you actually get more of the booking revenue, and it's slightly cheaper for the guest, so that's the main incentive.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: But does the direct bookings then reduce the nightly rate? ... How do you adjust [price] up and down?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Pricing software tracks the competitive set and aims for the top 10% of the local market; some of it is automated, some manually overridden because the software doesn't know what the property visually looks like.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: So who do you use for cleaning? [we already have a cleaning company we use for this house]
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: If you've already got a cleaner you know and trust who already does short-let cleaning, we're happy to use them — teams can go downhill, companies go bust, staff changes; one person you know and trust is usually better for everyone.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Okay, I can put you in touch with Zulaidi [Bright and Beautiful, Banbury franchise].

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Do you have any views on how we should furnish it? ... double beds in the three bedrooms and then a sofa bed in the bigger bedroom — is that sensible, or should we look to have twin beds in one of the rooms?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: If the bedrooms are big enough, get Zip and Link singles so the guest has maximum flexibility (three couples vs six individuals); if too tight for that, go double. Also recommended a desk/workspace since Airbnb actively highlights it as a feature.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Right... okay, fine, right. [sent photos via WhatsApp during the call]

lead_responses.what_lead_said: How long does it take to get set up? Do you do the photography? ... we're still a few weeks, not sure whether we want to push this to have it on the market for Christmas or let family use it over Christmas and start in January.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Get a key safe installed first (already done); assuming the property is handed over fully ready to short-let, realistically 2-3 weeks — cleaner on-site plus photographer, providing no delays in photography/editing or the cleaner.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: On a different property — we have a six-bed HMO in Northampton let to students until end of June next year, not on suites... is that the sort of thing we'd consider for this model? Would you do individual rooms in a property?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Would recommend letting it as a whole six-bed house rather than individual rooms — per-room competes against hotels on price and forces a race to the bottom; a whole-house listing tells a different story and could use a spare reception room as a games room if six-person sleeping capacity is tight.

conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Send a joint-readable written summary of the projections immediately (committed to within 30 minutes on this call) and offer to include the husband on any follow-up call

conversion_gaps.gap: No taxonomy code exists for a never-let new-build/conversion property deciding STL vs LTL before first occupation — filed under STL-SW as nearest fit only

conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Add a dedicated NEW-BUILD/DEV/CONV profile code (flagged repeatedly across prior entries, e.g. 039 Ben Lam, 101 Emily Moench)

Low local competition (44 avg reviews, 4.8 rating) framed as a realistic, fast path to the projected figures

zac_language.numbers_framing: Led with gross, then net, then the three deduction lines (commission, cleaning pass-through, management fee), then likely/worst/best case months so the lead sees the full range before any objection is raised
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Answers directly and concretely in-the-moment (fee structure, cleaning pass-through, pricing mechanics) rather than deferring, and volunteers corrections to his own presentation errors proactively post-call rather than letting them surface later

profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For a never-let new-build/conversion property, ask directly and early whether the build is fully finished (not just 'nearly'), since the qualification-vs-figures order matters less than usual here — the whole meeting is pre-decision, pre-furnishing groundwork rather than a live-property comparison
